Eternal OA SDE 2025 (On Campus, Intern + FTE)- 70 minutes 3 ques.
Q1. Given an array with at least one non-zero integer. A good array is an array, where the absolute difference between two adjacent elements is at max 1. All the 0’s of the arrays can be replaced by any integer. Find the number of possible good arrays.
eg . [0,0,1]
there are 9 possible ways to replace 0s and make a good array.
 
Q2. Given an array, where arr[i], means that task i is dependent on arr[i]. Find the minimum number of changes to be made to the array, such that there is exactly only one task which is dependent on itself, directly or indirectly.
eg. [1,2,3,4]
every task is dependent on itself -> change it to [1,1,1,1] -> 3 replacements

Q3. Given a tree, with n nodes numbered from 1 to n, each node has some stones. A good tree is a tree, in which, for all nodes, the difference in number of stones on any of its adjacent nodes is at max 1. Find the minimum number of stones you need to add to make the given tree a good tree. 
Input : 
tree_nodes : number of nodes
tree_from : node at one end of edge
tree_to : node at other end of edge
stones : containing stone at each node

Constrains , n <= 1000 , stones[i] <= 1000 ..

How to solve this type of problems ,,???

Think of them as a problem where there is a array , instead of tree.

1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 7 -> 5 -> 2

Now see suppose let us start our process from left , as we know greedy is not possible .  

Let us write our relations for ith index as 

    Base Case : dp[0][j] = (j >= stones[j]) ? (j - stones[j]) : INT_MIN

    if(j >= stones[i])

    dp[i][j] = (j - stones[i]) + min(dp[i - 1][j],dp[i - 1][j - 1],dp[i - 1][j + 1]);
